title: Gulshan i Raz, the Mystic Rose Garden
author: Mahmud Shabistari (Whinfield trans)
description: Gulshan i Raz: The Mystic Rose Garden of Sa'd ud din Mahmud Shabistari, the Persian text with an English translation and notes, chiefly from the commentary of Muhammad bin Yahya Lahiji, by E. H. Whinfield (London: Trübner, 1880). Whinfield, a judge of the Bengal Civil Service and translator of Rumi and Omar Khayyam, provides a scholarly line-by-line version of Shabistari's poem of about a thousand couplets, composed around 1317 in answer to fifteen questions on Sufi doctrine. Topics include the nature of thought, the journey of the soul from the many to the One, the Perfect Man, the 'I' and the illusion of separate existence, the unity of being after Ibn Arabi, and the hidden meanings of Sufi poetic imagery such as wine, the beloved's curl, cheek and eye, the tavern and the idol. Whinfield's introduction on Sufism and his notes from Lahiji's classic commentary make this the most useful scholarly English edition, complementing Lederer's devotional version in the library.
